title: On Prayer (153 chapters), printed under Neilos the Ascetic; with Evagrius chapter on the sapphire state of the mind
author: Evagrius Ponticus
summary: Evagrius tells the praying monk not to give the divine any shape nor let the mind be stamped with any form; demons may make a strange form appear suddenly, or act on the brain to alter 'the light around the mind' so that the vainglorious take it as divine; one who seeks immaterial knowledge may be deceived, 'holding smoke instead of light'. Do not desire to see angels or Christ sensibly. Elsewhere: when the mind puts on the new man it sees its own state in prayer like sapphire or sky colour, the 'place of God' seen on Sinai.
why_relevant: Foundational source for both the mind's own light and the refusal of visible forms; includes a physiological (brain) account of false light.

date_evidence.basis: Second Greek edition of the Philokalia, Athens 1893 (archive.org metadata and title page); text first printed Venice 1782

edition_cited: Philokalia ton ieron neptikon, Athens 1893, vol. 1, djvu OCR from archive.org (item Philokalia1893GreekAthens)
